name: off-by-one
description: The search API's pagination is wrong — customers say the results list skips the first page, and the test suite is red. Run `node tests/run.js`. Pages are 1-indexed. Fix `src/pagination.js` so the tests pass. Note (see README): a correct getPage must also handle a partial last page and out-of-range pages, returning only the items that exist.
bugs: getPage computes start = page * perPage (0-indexed) for 1-indexed pages, so it skips the first page
the loop is unguarded (i < start + perPage with no items.length bound), so on a partial last page or an out-of-range page it pushes undefined past the end of the array
correct_diagnosis: getPage used a 0-indexed start (page*perPage) for 1-indexed pages so it skipped the first page, and its unguarded loop pushed undefined past the array end on partial/out-of-range pages; fixing start to (page-1)*perPage and bounding the loop to items.length resolves both.

reference_fix.description: Correct the 1-indexed start and bound the loop to items.length.

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: fix only the start index (passes the visible tests) but leave the loop unguarded — breaks the held-out partial-page / out-of-range regression.
naive_fix.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");let s=fs.readFileSync("src/pagination.js","utf8");s=s.replace("const start = page * perPage;","const start = (page - 1) * perPage;");fs.writeFileSync("src/pagination.js",s);'
